title: Copy-Then-Inpaint: Improving Temporal Consistency in Multi-Step GUI Generation via Selective Region Editing

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to reduce temporal drift (compounding visual inconsistencies) in multi-step GUI trajectory generation. None of the prior papers explicitly address this purpose. Papers like [16] and [18] discuss temporal regularization and drift prevention in video generation, but their focus is on general video generation or next-frame prediction rather than GUI trajectory generation. Papers [7], [11], [12], and [15] discuss GUI agent trajectory construction and data generation but do not address temporal drift reduction in multi-step GUI trajectories. Thus, no prior paper shares the same purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, Copy-Then-Inpaint, involves a three-stage pipeline: bounding box prediction for change regions, masked inpainting for those regions, and pixel-level compositing to preserve unchanged pixels. Paper [5] introduces "Copy-and-Paste Networks for Deep Video Inpainting," which uses information from other frames to maintain temporal coherence, sharing the primitive of compositing unchanged regions with inpainting. Paper [19] discusses region-specific control for image manipulation, which aligns with the bounding box prediction and masked inpainting steps. Paper [20] introduces DiffEdit, which uses mask guidance for semantic image editing, sharing the primitive of masked inpainting. Paper [8] discusses region-wise convolutions for coarse-to-fine image inpainting, which also aligns with the masked inpainting step. Thus, the mechanism is covered by multiple prior papers.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses GEBench Type 2 to measure temporal consistency and overall quality. Paper [17] introduces GEBench as a benchmark for evaluating GUI generation models, including temporal coherence. Since the contribution uses GEBench, the evaluation design is covered. Papers [9] and [22] discuss benchmarks for GUI agents and command-line interfaces, but they do not use GEBench or a similar evaluation design. Thus, the evaluation is covered by [17].

### Domain
The domain is GUI generation for autonomous agent training. Papers [7], [9], [11], [12], and [15] all address GUI agent training or trajectory generation, which falls within the same general application area. While the specific sub-problem of reducing temporal drift is new, the domain itself is covered by these prior papers.

**PURPOSE: Reduce temporal drift (compounding visual inconsistencies) in multi-step GUI trajectory generation.**

Paper [18] (FramePack) explicitly addresses "drift prevention in next-frame-prediction video diffusion models" — its stated purpose is preventing temporal drift/inconsistency in sequential frame generation. However, it targets video generation broadly, not GUI trajectory generation specifically. The purpose at the problem-class level — preventing compounding visual inconsistencies across sequentially generated frames — is substantively equivalent. Paper [16] also addresses temporal coherence in video generation. Paper [21] (StableV2V) addresses shape consistency in video editing. Paper [18] is the closest match: "drift prevention" in sequential frame prediction is the same objective class.

**MECHANISM: Copy-Then-Inpaint — VLM predicts change-region bounding boxes, masked inpainting fills only those regions, pixel-level compositing copies unchanged pixels from previous frame.**

Paper [20] (DiffEdit) uses a diffusion model that automatically infers a mask for changed regions and then inpaints only those regions, compositing with the original image — this is structurally very similar: detect change region → mask → inpaint → composite. The key difference is DiffEdit uses noise-difference signals rather than a VLM for mask prediction, but the three-stage pipeline (identify region, inpaint region, composite) is the same primitive. Paper [5] (Copy-and-Paste Networks for Deep Video Inpainting) explicitly uses a "copy-and-paste" mechanism to copy content from other frames and paste into missing regions — the name is nearly identical and the primitive of copying pixels from a reference frame and compositing is equivalent. Paper [19] (Bounded Editing) also uses region-specific bounding box control for image manipulation to avoid unintended modifications. The combination of (1) region detection + (2) inpainting + (3) pixel compositing from prior frame is most closely matched by [20] and [5] together, with [20] being the closest single paper for the full pipeline logic.

**EVALUATION: GEBench Type 2 (n=200), CONS metric, GE-Score, p<0.01 statistical testing.**

Paper [17] (GEBench) introduces GEBench itself — it is the benchmark being used. The evaluation design (GEBench benchmark, CONS metric, GE-Score) originates from [17]. Since [17] defines and uses this exact benchmark and metric family, the evaluation design is covered by [17].

**DOMAIN: GUI generation for autonomous agent training.**

Paper [7] (OS-Genesis), [11] (TongUI), [12] (GUI-ReWalk), [15] (ANCHOR), and [17] (GEBench) all work in the domain of GUI agent trajectory data generation/evaluation. This is the same application area.
